$comment: The hand-written half of this project's manifest. Everything else -- sizes, hashes, the firmware ABI, the display name -- is derived from the built bytes by scripts/make_manifest.py. This release publishes the binary and its metadata only: OpenLara needs Tomb Raider level data the user already owns, converted from PHD to PKD, and that converter is not yet a wasm module, so there is no tool to declare and nothing here claims to produce those files. dataDir is what this project exists to state. src/platform/gnw/os.cpp searches a fixed list of paths for <name>.PKD and every one of them sits under a folder literally spelled 'openlara' -- /homebrews/openlara, /homebrews/openlara/fmv, /homebrews/openlara/data. That name is compiled into the binary and matches neither PACKED_BIN (OpenLara.bin) nor HB_NAME (OpenLara), so nothing can derive it. originalSystem is omitted deliberately: OpenLara is a port of an open-source reimplementation of the Tomb Raider engine, not of any one console release. Tomb Raider 1 shipped on PlayStation, Saturn and DOS at once and the data this reads is whichever of those the user owns, so the field exists to point an art scraper at one library and there is no single right answer to give it. Same reasoning as pong.
